sources.name: Kelvon Ochoa
sources.quote: Working at Anthropic, I've seen the company grow steadily, but what stands out is how it's become part of the neighborhood's rhythm. You see more familiar faces at the coffee shops in the morning—colleagues grabbing their caffeine before heading in. There's a quiet pride in being part of something that's both local and global in impact. The Construction Authority's work is more visible, of course—you can't miss the scaffolding and new facades—but both businesses feel like they're putting down roots here.

sources.name: Brianna Lee
sources.quote: You know, working at Baylight Construction Authority, I see the growth firsthand—not just in the numbers, but in the way the neighborhood feels. More people stopping by the coffee shops before heading to work, more faces I don't recognize but nod to anyway. There's a buzz, especially around Anthropic—folks in tech wear walking alongside us in hardhats. It's not just buildings going up; it's the kind of energy that makes you feel like the district's alive, you know?

sources.name: Tariq Jello
sources.quote: You know, working over at Baylight Construction Authority, I see those Anthropic folks coming and going. They've got that new building going up near the old rail yard - sleek thing, all glass and steel. Different crowd than us blue-collar types, but they keep our coffee shops busy. Funny how the neighborhood's changing - still got the same old problems with the plumbing though, no matter how fancy the offices get.

approvedQuotes.text: Working at Anthropic, I've seen the company grow steadily, but what stands out is how it's become part of the neighborhood's rhythm. You see more familiar faces at the coffee shops in the morning—colleagues grabbing their caffeine before heading in. There's a quiet pride in being part of something that's both local and global in impact. The Construction Authority's work is more visible, of course—you can't miss the scaffolding and new facades—but both businesses feel like they're putting down roots here.

You know, working at Baylight Construction Authority, I see the growth firsthand—not just in the numbers, but in the way the neighborhood feels. More people stopping by the coffee shops before heading to work, more faces I don't recognize but nod to anyway. There's a buzz, especially around Anthropic—folks in tech wear walking alongside us in hardhats. It's not just buildings going up; it's the kind of energy that makes you feel like the district's alive, you know?

You know, working over at Baylight Construction Authority, I see those Anthropic folks coming and going. They've got that new building going up near the old rail yard - sleek thing, all glass and steel. Different crowd than us blue-collar types, but they keep our coffee shops busy. Funny how the neighborhood's changing - still got the same old problems with the plumbing though, no matter how fancy the offices get.
